newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs firm on shortage of prompt ships.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs firm on shortage of prompt ships.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates from the Middle East firmed on Tuesday, boosted by a shortage of vessels for prompt dates, brokers said.
"If you're looking for a vessel up to (May) 20th, you're likely to get stuck. It's very hard to find ships for promptish dates," one broker said.

Brokers said 250,000 tonne VLCCs on Mideast/west voyages were fixed at W55, up five points from late last week, with trips to Japan at W60 or slightly more. Last month Mideast VLCC rates fell as low as W45.
The 260,000 tonne Sabang was reported fixed at W61.5 Mideast/Japan for Toktank, while the 330,000 tonne Jahre Pollux was said done at W50 Ras Tanura/St Johns for Irving.
The West Africa market was also looking slightly stronger, with VLCCs to the U.S. Gulf fixed around W67.5 and 130,000 tonne (million barrel) ships at W97.5.
"The reason's quite simple -- a good number of cargoes and not so many ships available," a broker said.
The transatlantic market was steady, with 250,000 tonnes North Sea/USAC assessed around W65. The 265,000 tonne Stena Congress was said fixed at W61.5 Mongstad/USG for Statoil.
In the Mediterranean, the million-barrel market was steady to firm at W90/92.5 in parallel with West Africa. "The market seems to be good...It won't go down for now," said an Italian broker.

But he said the Med 80,000 tonne (Aframax) market was looking soft at W105 or lower, pushed down by a lack of cargoes and plenty of offers for the few vessels on offer. "The next ship will be fixed lower (than W105)," he predicted.
The inter-U.K./Cont Aframax market also showed a soft tone at about W90, depressed by a lack of enquiry, another broker said.

Fuel oil fell too, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont around W170 and cross-Med at W175, both some 15 points down from late last week. One broker said this reflected a growing market for 50,000 tonne stems.
In the Western hemisphere, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes were steady at W175, while 50,000 fuel oil stems firmed to W185 from W170. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
